name: DeviceCheck two bits
plain: Apple stores two bits per device per developer on its servers.
meaning: Lets a developer mark a device (for example, trial used) with 2 bits that persist across reinstall and device wipe; no other data.

android.note: Play Integrity gives verdicts, not storage

ios.persistence: Cannot be cleared by the user
ios.api_surface: 2 bits plus last update month; per developer account; server to server with an Apple key

limits.headline: Can store two yes or no flags about your device on Apple's servers
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app's server asks Apple about your device
can: Set or look up 2 bits on Apple's servers for this device and this developer
Remember a device was flagged (for example, a used free trial) even after you reinstall
Learn the month the bits were last changed
cannot: Store anything beyond 2 bits and a date
Share the bits with other developers
See your Apple ID, name or any personal detail
Work on Android; there is no equivalent
limits.differs: Only iPhone has DeviceCheck. Android gives integrity verdicts but no storage.

story.what_it_is: Apple lets an app store two private yes or no flags about your phone on its servers.

marketing.name: DeviceCheck
marketing.pitch: Apple offers two bits per device so developers can remember simple things like a used free trial.

story.for_you: You never see it. It can mean that if you used a free trial once, the app may still know after you delete it and reinstall. You cannot clear it yourself.
story.for_makers: Makers use these two bits to stop people from claiming a free trial again and again, or to mark a phone that abused a promo. It survives reinstall and even a wipe of the device, which is why it works so well for abuse control.

use_cases.example: A music streaming app marks your phone when you finish a free trial so a new email cannot get another one.
A mobile game flags a phone that abused a gift code so the same phone cannot claim it again on a new account.
A dating app remembers that a phone was banned for harassment, so a fresh profile does not slip through.
A store limits a welcome coupon to one claim per phone even after an app reinstall.
An ad network flags a device that produced fake installs, then discounts its traffic.
A bank app marks a phone used in a known scam so later sign ins from it get extra checks.

story.android_note: Android has no exact twin. Developers use Play Integrity and server side checks instead.
story.ios_note: This is Apple only. Each developer gets its own two bits per device, so it cannot link different developers.
